newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul to oppose conglomerate banking role - paper.
newsitem.headline: Seoul to oppose conglomerate banking role - paper.

text.p: South Korea's finance ministry plans to oppose a recommendation by a presidential commission for big conglomerates to participate in bank management, the Korea Economic Daily reported on Monday.
The commission, composed of bankers, academics and business officials, is looking into reform of the financial industry and is expected to make its formal recommendations on Monday.
Finance ministry officials were not immediately available to comment on the report, which brokers said was likely to dampen buying interest in banking shares.
Commission members have said one of their proposals is to allow representatives of the nation's top five conglomerates to sit on bank boards as non-permanent directors.
South Korea currently bans conglomerates, known as chaebol, from bank management because of fears of growing economic concentration. -- Seoul Newsroom (822) 727 5645
